scenes.title: tensor — one element, one lattice
scenes.description: Three 6×6 lattices, one per way of supplying values: live, static, and baked.
scenes.markdown:
# `tensor`

Each grid below is **one element**, not 36.

**Left — `valueExpr`, live.** One expression, evaluated per cell with `row` and `col` bound. Row $i$ is a softmax over $s_{ij} = e^{-|i-j|\cdot k}$, so every row sums to 1. Drag **sharpness** and watch it go from uniform to near-diagonal.

**Middle — `values`, static.** Literal numbers, built once, **zero** per-frame cost: a causal mask, the shape that makes parallel training legal.

**Right — `dataTable`, baked.** Also one `valueExpr`, but it reads a table in the scene's `data` block rather than computing from a formula:

```
dataTable('attn', row, concat('w', col))
```

This is how a real lesson supplies numbers — the weights come from a model and are baked into the JSON, so nothing is invented at render time and every value is reproducible offline. This head attends mostly to the **previous token**, partly to **position 0**, and never to the future.

**Sharpness reshapes the baked head too**, by $p_j^{\,k}$ renormalized over each row. At $k \to 0$ it flattens to uniform *over what the head is allowed to see* — the zeros stay zero, so no attention leaks into the future. At $k=1$ it is the stored head unchanged; above that it concentrates further.

**Below the baked head** — the same data at rank 1. `shape: [6]` draws a vector rather than a matrix through the same code path, tracks row 3 of the matrix above, and takes its axis labels from `axes` rather than hand-placed `text` elements.

Cell geometry is arithmetic on `shape`, not expressions, so nothing is re-evaluated for positions that never move.

**Bottom — the other channels.** Value drives colour by default; `widthExpr` and `heightExpr` make it drive size too (here `sqrt(value)` on both, so cell *area* is the weight), and `textExpr` prints the number inside the cell, fitted to whatever size the cell currently has. The row beside it uses `heightExpr` alone with `anchor: "bottom"`: a bar chart standing on its lattice.

steps.title: Three ways to fill a lattice
steps.description: Drag **sharpness** $k$: the live grid, the baked head and its row all respond. Only the **mask** is static — it has literal `values`, so it registers no per-frame work at all.

add.valueExpr: (exp(-abs(row - col) * sharp)) / (exp(-abs(row - 0) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 1) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 2) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 3) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 4) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 5) * sharp))
add.label: live · valueExpr
add.prompt: A row-stochastic matrix computed live: each row is a softmax over scores that decay with distance from the diagonal. Explain why every row sums to 1 and what the sharpness slider does to the distribution.

add.label: static · values
add.prompt: A causal mask: cell (i,j) is 1 when j <= i. Explain why masking the future is what makes it legal to train on every position of a sequence in a single parallel forward pass.

add.valueExpr: (dataTable('attn', row, concat('w', col))^max(sharp, 0.001)) / (dataTable('attn', row, 'w0')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', row, 'w1')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', row, 'w2')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', row, 'w3')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', row, 'w4')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', row, 'w5')^max(sharp, 0.001))
add.label: baked · dataTable
add.prompt: This attention pattern is read from the scene's data block with dataTable, not computed from a formula. It attends mostly to the previous token, partly to position 0, and never to the future. Explain what a previous-token head does and why an attention sink at position 0 shows up in real models.

add.valueExpr: (dataTable('attn', 3, concat('w', col))^max(sharp, 0.001)) / (dataTable('attn', 3, 'w0')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', 3, 'w1')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', 3, 'w2')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', 3, 'w3')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', 3, 'w4')^max(sharp, 0.001) + dataTable('attn', 3, 'w5')^max(sharp, 0.001))
add.label: 1D · rank-1 view
add.prompt: This is row 3 of the matrix above, drawn on its own as a rank-1 tensor. Explain that a row of an attention matrix is a probability distribution over the earlier tokens, and what the sharpness control is doing to that distribution.

add.valueExpr: exp(-abs(row - col) * sharp) / (exp(-abs(row - 0) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 1) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 2) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 3) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 4) * sharp) + exp(-abs(row - 5) * sharp))
add.label: sized + labelled
add.prompt: The live softmax matrix again, with two more channels: each cell is drawn sqrt(value) wide and tall, so its AREA is the weight, and its value is printed inside it, fitted to the shrunken cell.

add.valueExpr: exp(-abs(3 - col) * sharp) / (exp(-abs(3 - 0) * sharp) + exp(-abs(3 - 1) * sharp) + exp(-abs(3 - 2) * sharp) + exp(-abs(3 - 3) * sharp) + exp(-abs(3 - 4) * sharp) + exp(-abs(3 - 5) * sharp))
add.label: row 3 as bars
add.prompt: Row 3 of the live matrix as a bar chart: heightExpr is the value itself, anchor is bottom so every bar stands on the same baseline, width is untouched, and the number rides inside each bar.

info.content:
**Live** row 0 sums to $1.000$ by construction.

$\alpha_{00} = {{ (exp(0) / (exp(0) + exp(-1*sharp) + exp(-2*sharp) + exp(-3*sharp) + exp(-4*sharp) + exp(-5*sharp))) }}$

**Baked** row 3 *as stored* in `data` — what the grid shows is this, re-sharpened by $k$ (equal at $k=1$):

$\alpha_{3,2} = {{ dataTable('attn', 3, 'w2') }}$, $\alpha_{3,0} = {{ dataTable('attn', 3, 'w0') }}$, $\alpha_{3,5} = {{ dataTable('attn', 3, 'w5') }}$
